BUS.G12.T1.LEGISLATION.A1.title: Impact of recent legislation on business
BUS.G12.T1.LEGISLATION.A1.description: The impact of recent legislation, developed for redress and equity, on small and large business: the Skills Development Act, Labour Relations Act, Employment Equity Act, Basic Conditions of Employment Act, COIDA, BEE and BBBEE, National Credit Act and Consumer Protection Act, plus human rights, inclusivity and environmental issues.
BUS.G12.T1.LEGISLATION.A1.strand: T1 — Legislation, Human Resources, ethics, creative thinking & business strategies
BUS.G12.T1.LEGISLATION.A1.recovery_strategy: Tie each Act to its purpose: EEA = fair, equal workplaces; BCEA = minimum working conditions; LRA = fair labour relations and unions; SDA = skills and SETAs; CPA = consumer rights; NCA = fair credit; BBBEE = economic redress; COIDA = injury compensation.

questions.question: What does the Employment Equity Act (EEA) mainly promote?
options: Equity and protection from unfair discrimination at work
questions.expected: Equity and protection from unfair discrimination at work
questions.memo: The EEA promotes equal opportunity and fair treatment, prohibiting unfair discrimination in the workplace.

questions.question: The Basic Conditions of Employment Act (BCEA) mainly sets:
options: Minimum working conditions such as hours and leave
questions.expected: Minimum working conditions such as hours and leave
questions.memo: The BCEA sets minimum employment conditions — working hours, leave, notice and similar protections.

questions.question: Which Act compensates employees who are injured or fall ill at work?
questions.expected: COIDA
questions.memo: COIDA — the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act — pays compensation to workers injured or made ill on the job.

questions.question: True or false: Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment (BBBEE) aims to redress past economic inequality.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: BBBEE seeks to redress the economic imbalances of the past by broadening participation in the economy.

questions.question: The _________ Protection Act protects the rights of consumers.
questions.expected: Consumer
questions.memo: The Consumer Protection Act (CPA) protects consumers' rights to fair, safe and honest treatment.

questions.question: True or false: The Skills Development Act supports training, funded through a skills levy and SETAs.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: The Skills Development Act funds and coordinates training through the skills levy and Sector Education and Training Authorities (SETAs).

questions.question: Sort each Act under the area it mainly deals with.
questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: BCEA and LRA govern the workplace; NCA and CPA protect consumers and credit users; EEA and SDA address equity and skills.

questions.question: What does the Labour Relations Act (LRA) mainly govern?
options: Fair labour relations, including unions and disputes
The interest rate on home loans
questions.expected: Fair labour relations, including unions and disputes
questions.memo: The LRA governs the relationship between employers, employees and unions, covering bargaining, strikes and dispute resolution.

questions.question: Read the case and select the parts that show legislation affecting the business.
questions.source_text: A manufacturer reviews its obligations. It must register staff for injury compensation under COIDA and pay the skills levy that funds SETA training. Its head office was recently repainted, and it has set fair, non-discriminatory hiring rules to meet the Employment Equity Act.
questions.task: Tap the parts that show legislation affecting the business.

targets.phrase: register staff for injury compensation under COIDA
targets.reason: COIDA is legislation requiring injury cover.

targets.phrase: pay the skills levy that funds SETA training
targets.reason: The skills levy comes from the Skills Development Act.

targets.phrase: set fair, non-discriminatory hiring rules to meet the Employment Equity Act
targets.reason: The EEA requires fair, non-discriminatory employment.

questions.expected: register staff for injury compensation under COIDA; pay the skills levy that funds SETA training; set fair, non-discriminatory hiring rules to meet the Employment Equity Act
questions.memo: COIDA, the skills levy (SDA) and the EEA are all legislation shaping the business. Repainting the office is not a legal obligation.

questions.question: BBBEE stands for Broad-Based Black _________ Empowerment.
questions.expected: Economic
questions.memo: BBBEE is Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment, aimed at broadening economic participation.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the National Credit Act (NCA)?
options: To protect consumers in credit agreements and promote responsible lending
questions.expected: To protect consumers in credit agreements and promote responsible lending
questions.memo: The NCA protects consumers who buy on credit and requires lenders to lend responsibly.

questions.question: True or false: The Consumer Protection Act gives consumers the right to fair, safe and honest treatment.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: The CPA protects consumers' rights to safe products, honest information and fair business practice.

questions.question: Sort each item into whether it is mainly a cost of compliance or a benefit of the legislation.

items.text: A better-skilled workforce from SETA training
Extra admin to meet equity reporting

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Legislation brings compliance costs (levies, admin, contributions) but also real benefits (skills, fairness, worker protection).

questions.question: How does the Skills Development Act, through SETAs, benefit business?
options: It funds and coordinates training to build a more skilled workforce
It lowers the price of raw materials
It removes the need to pay any tax
questions.expected: It funds and coordinates training to build a more skilled workforce
questions.memo: The SDA uses the skills levy and SETAs to fund training, helping businesses access better-skilled workers.

questions.question: Human rights in the Constitution include the rights to:
questions.expected: Equality, dignity and fair treatment
questions.memo: Constitutional human rights include equality, human dignity and fair treatment, which businesses must respect.

questions.question: Read the case and select the examples of INCLUSIVITY and human-rights measures.
questions.source_text: A company updates its policies. It makes its building wheelchair-accessible for staff with disabilities and adopts a hiring policy that welcomes people of all races and genders. It also buys a new delivery van and repaints the canteen.
questions.task: Tap the parts that show inclusivity or human-rights measures.

targets.phrase: makes its building wheelchair-accessible for staff with disabilities
targets.reason: Accessibility for disabled staff is an inclusivity/human-rights measure.

targets.phrase: adopts a hiring policy that welcomes people of all races and genders
targets.reason: Inclusive, non-discriminatory hiring reflects equity and human rights.

questions.expected: makes its building wheelchair-accessible for staff with disabilities; adopts a hiring policy that welcomes people of all races and genders
questions.memo: Accessibility and inclusive hiring are inclusivity and human-rights measures. Buying a van and repainting the canteen are not.

questions.question: An employee is dismissed without a fair hearing. Which Act most directly applies?
questions.expected: The Labour Relations Act (LRA)
questions.memo: Unfair dismissal is a labour-relations matter governed by the LRA, which requires fair procedures.

questions.question: How does redress-and-equity legislation typically affect small versus large businesses?
options: It adds compliance costs and admin, which can weigh more heavily on small businesses, while promoting fairer workplaces overall
It has no effect on any business
It only ever benefits businesses with no costs
It applies only to large businesses and never to small ones
questions.expected: It adds compliance costs and admin, which can weigh more heavily on small businesses, while promoting fairer workplaces overall
questions.memo: Compliance has real costs that can press harder on small firms, even as the legislation makes workplaces fairer and more inclusive for everyone.

questions.question: Why was legislation such as the EEA and BBBEE introduced?
options: To redress past inequality and create fairer access to the economy
To raise the price of consumer goods
questions.expected: To redress past inequality and create fairer access to the economy
questions.memo: These Acts respond to demands for redress and equity, broadening fair participation in the workplace and economy.

questions.question: A retailer sells a customer a dangerous, faulty appliance and refuses a refund. Which Act protects the customer, and how?
options: The Consumer Protection Act — it gives the right to safe goods and fair redress
The Skills Development Act — it trains the customer
The Labour Relations Act — it governs the sale
questions.expected: The Consumer Protection Act — it gives the right to safe goods and fair redress
questions.memo: The CPA protects consumers' rights to safe products and fair treatment, including remedies such as refunds for defective goods.
